mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the rise in UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in one month signals a strengthening supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with subsequent economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPIAUCSL YoY is below 2%, the real interest rate is high, signaling a restrictive monetary policy that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and low CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
regime_hint: tight labor market with strong job growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of low UNRATE and high PAYEMS does not correlate with subsequent economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and industrial production (INDPRO) is also declining, it signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 consecutive quarters and INDPRO declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of negative GDPC1 and declining INDPRO does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction.
